title: Ribollita: Tuscan Bean, Cavolo Nero and Bread Soup
summary: A thick, rustic Tuscan soup of cannellini beans, cavolo nero, tomatoes and soffritto, thickened with toasted bread that is whisked in until creamy. Finished with a generous drizzle of good olive oil.
equipment: large casserole (at least 5 litres) with a lid

ingredients.item: day-old rustic white bread, crusts removed, torn into 2-3 cm pieces
extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
cavolo nero or kale, tough stems removed, leaves sliced 1 cm wide
fine sea salt or table salt
tinned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, with their juice
ingredients.note: two 400 g tins, no salt added

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Spread the bread over the tray in a single layer and bake for about 10 minutes, stirring once, until dry and lightly golden. Drying the bread helps it soak up the broth and break down into a creamy texture rather than turning gluey.

steps.title: Soften the soffritto
steps.text: While the bread toasts, heat the 80 ml oil in the casserole over medium-high heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery and salt and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring, until softened. Stir in the garlic and chilli flakes for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes and their juice and cook for about 2 minutes, until slightly thickened. A brief cook takes the raw edge off the tomatoes and concentrates their flavour before the liquid goes in.

steps.title: Simmer the greens
steps.text: Stir in the stock, water, beans and cavolo nero and bring to a simmer. Lower the heat to medium-low, cover and cook for about 10 minutes, until the greens are tender. Cavolo nero holds its texture well, so it stays pleasantly silky rather than mushy.

steps.title: Whisk in the bread
steps.text: Stir in the toasted bread, cover and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Take the pot off the heat and whisk vigorously for about 2 minutes, until the bread breaks down and the soup turns thick and creamy. The starch from the bread thickens the soup into its signature spoon-standing consistency.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Taste and add a little more salt or chilli if needed. Ladle into bowls and drizzle each with olive oil. The raw oil adds a fresh, peppery richness that ties everything together.

tips: Use a firm rustic loaf; soft sandwich bread dissolves into paste.
A common mistake is skipping the whisking; without it the bread stays in soggy lumps instead of thickening the soup.
Ribollita is even better reheated the next day, which is how it got its name.
Use cavolo nero if you can find it, as it holds its shape better than curly kale.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water as it thickens, until piping hot (74 °C). Freezing is not recommended once the bread is added. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
